# Steady Scale

> A privacy-first iPhone weight-tracking app that uses statistical trend analysis to separate the underlying trend from day-to-day fluctuations, so people can understand whether their weight is really changing instead of reacting to daily noise. No accounts, no ads, no gamification. Supports weight loss, gain, and maintenance.

Steady Scale is designed more like a scientific measurement instrument than a social or engagement-driven app. It averages multiple weigh-ins per day and fits a 14-day rolling Ridge (L2-regularized) regression to estimate the underlying weight trend, then projects a goal date with an honest, widening uncertainty range. Data is stored on the user's device with optional private iCloud backup. It is a subscription app ($1.99/month or $14.99/year) with a 7-day free trial, iPhone-only.

Built in Ottawa, Canada by Ryan Groome (experimental physicist, PhD) and Eveline Soares Menezes (kinesiologist, PhD).

## Core pages

- [How it works](https://steadyscale.app/how-it-works): the method — daily averaging, the 14-day trend, plan target vs. trend forecast, the goal-date projection and uncertainty cone.
- [The science](https://steadyscale.app/science): the research and statistical model behind the app, with peer-reviewed citations and honest limitations.
- [Quick guide](https://steadyscale.app/guide): short answers — reading the chart, choosing a goal and rate, why weight fluctuates day to day, how data is handled.
- [About](https://steadyscale.app/about): who builds Steady Scale (a physicist and a kinesiologist).

## Key concepts

- Body weight fluctuates day to day mostly because of water, food, and digestion, not fat — most short-term change is fat-free mass.
- A weight *trend* (rolling average) is more informative than any single daily weigh-in.
- Steady Scale separates signal (the trend) from noise (daily fluctuation) using statistical smoothing rather than reacting to each reading.
- Privacy-first: on-device storage, optional private iCloud backup, no accounts, no ads, no analytics, no streaks or engagement mechanics.
